chunks: And from him, from Muhammad ibn Sayf ibn 'Amirah, from Mansur ibn Hazim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
I asked him about the two rak'ahs of the obligatory Tawaf. He said, 'Do not delay them for an hour when you have performed Tawaf, so pray them.'

And it has been narrated that it is disliked to do so when the sun is yellowing (setting) and when it is rising. The primary ruling in this matter is what we mentioned, and due to what was narrated from them (peace be upon him) that they said: 'Five prayers are to be prayed at all times, among them are the two rak'ahs of Tawaf.' And the one who narrated the dislike of what we mentioned.

key_terms.إِصْفِرَارُ الشَّمْسِ: The yellowing of the sun (time of sunset)
key_terms.رَكْعَتَا الطَّوَافِ: The two rak'ahs of prayer performed after Tawaf

ai.seo_question: When should the two rak'ahs of Tawaf prayer be performed after completing the circumambulation?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes the immediate performance of the two rak'ahs of Tawaf as the primary ruling, overriding narrations that suggest dislike for delaying them during specific times like sunrise or sunset. This precedence is grounded in the principle that these two units are intrinsically linked to the five daily obligatory prayers, ensuring their timely observance regardless of temporal nuances.
